parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, facility rule, custody rule, border practice or enforcement measure is documented, and same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2014 — so the traveller faces no known state-imposed exposure. The rubric's resident-facing gaps (no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination statute, constitutional marriage bar) are not visitor exposures and must not be deducted; the marriage point affects residents and partners, not the visitor's own safety. Positive climate signals: SOGI joint statement (2011), accepted UPR recommendations, presidential equality statement. But the record is thin and entirely silent on border questioning, facilities, custody, care and social attitudes — silence here is not evidence of safety, so this sits below the reduced-risk anchors that document actual acceptance and working remedies. Extrapolating from a conservative-but-reforming legal order with no documented hostility yields a rating just above the midpoint.
